summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of recurrent DKA was admitted for hyperglycemia, nausea, vomiting, and chronic back pain. She was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis and managed in the ICU with an insulin drip and fluid resuscitation. Her condition improved with transition to subcutaneous insulin, and she was moved to the medical floor. Treatment included restarting H. pylori therapy for gastritis, managing nausea with metoclopramide, and addressing back pain with acetaminophen, tramadol, and a lidocaine patch. Psychiatric comorbidities were acknowledged, and a plan for outpatient mental health support and visiting nurses was established. She was discharged home with services, on stable insulin therapy, antibiotics, and pain management, with follow-up arranged for diabetes, GI, and physical therapy.
